summary.text: Maxine Dexter is the Democratic nominee for re-election to Oregon's 3rd Congressional District, which she has represented since 2025. A pulmonary and critical-care physician, she spent more than 15 years at Kaiser Permanente before serving in the Oregon House of Representatives from 2020 to 2024, where she chaired the Housing and Homelessness Committee.

paragraphs.text: Maxine Dexter was born in Seattle, Washington, in 1972 and grew up in the Pacific Northwest in a working-class family; according to her official biography, she took a union job at Albertsons at 16 and became the first in her family to graduate from college.

She earned a bachelor's degree in political science and communications in 1997 and an M.D. in 2001, both from the University of Washington, and Ballotpedia lists her as triple-boarded in internal medicine, pulmonology and critical care medicine.
After her medical training she moved to Portland with her husband and two children and practiced for over 15 years as a lung and critical-care physician at Kaiser Permanente.
Her physician group elected her to leadership roles, and she became the first woman to chair the Board of Directors at Northwest Permanente.
Dexter has been a member of the Oregon Medical Association and a trustee of the Tualatin Hills Park Foundation.

She was appointed in 2020 to Oregon House District 33, succeeding Mitch Greenlick, and served through 2024; as chair of the House Housing and Homelessness Committee she led passage of a multi-billion-dollar housing and homelessness bill, and she also worked on abortion access, addiction treatment, public lands and gun-violence legislation.
She was elected to the U.S. House in 2024, succeeding Earl Blumenauer.
In Congress she serves on the Veterans' Affairs and Natural Resources committees and is Ranking Member of the Natural Resources Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
